parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` and `MainActorNotificationMessage` in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/` share three of three members: `name: Notification.Name`, `makeNotification(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification`, and `makeMessage(_ notification: Notification) -> Self?`. The only structural difference is the `sending` ownership annotation on `MainActorNotificationMessage`'s `makeMessage` parameter, which reflects a concurrency-domain distinction rather than a semantic one. Introducing a parent PAT `NotificationMessage` with the shared contract (`name`, `makeNotification`, and a base `makeMessage`) and letting each child protocol refine `makeMessage` with its own concurrency annotation would eliminate the duplicated surface while preserving the actor-isolation distinction. Both protocols live in the same `Core` package with no restraint markers, making this a clean consolidation opportunity.
